title: AI Datasets
answer: Training and evaluation datasets with size, licence, provenance, language coverage, and documented bias.

reading.body:
The dataset layer of AI breaks into three parts, and the smallest of them by count is training data.

Training datasets number 8, evaluation datasets 9, and licensing and provenance 17. The pattern is that the legal and documentary work around data outnumbers the data itself. Licensing and provenance is the largest group by more than double either of the other two.

That matters because data is the input that compute consumes, and the terms on which it may be consumed are settled before a model is trained, not after. A corpus with unclear provenance is not a smaller corpus, it is an unusable one. The counts here suggest the field spends more effort establishing what may lawfully be used than cataloguing what exists.

This data does not cover dataset size, language coverage, or documented bias, despite the description naming all three. It gives counts of entries in three categories and nothing about their contents. It also does not say whether the imbalance reflects the state of the field or the state of the catalogue.
